div.div: This can happen due to a safety mechanism leading to a device reset (machine check reset, error controller reset, watchdog, power reset etc.) or if the Error Controller automatically floats all I/O pins.

div.div: The STRICT_SAFE_STATE feature ensures all I/O pins are floated even if peripherals and PORT has been initialized during Startup and releases the force float all at once, ensuring a strict transition between the Safe State and Mission Mode. When disabled, the system will more gradually transition into Mission Mode while still in Startup as peripherals are initialized in the application startup schedule.

div.div: Safe State is strictly defined as a device state where all I/O pins are floated so that the device cannot impact the outside world (given that the surrounding circuitry handles this situation). A device reset should always lead to a Safe State. Mission Mode is defined as any situation where the system is not in a Safe State, which typically is when the device is running the application.
